column1: # Specified by The Designer, Step 1 Wave 2 review section 3.3; accepted by The Manager at the
# Step 1 close, decision 5.2. Built and loaded at sub-step 1.14 by The Engineer.
# quantity-id is written BARE, without brackets, so tools/quantities.js does not read this
# column as a quotation tag. oracle/** is inside the counting rule's declared file set.
#   AM-1 no two rows with state:owed name the same non-"-" quantity id
#   AM-2 every superseded-by resolves to a row that is not itself superseded
#   AM-3 every target is a row in oracle/MANIFEST.tsv
#   AM-4 no row is applied while its target's manifest row reads specified

column9: ABORT is defined twice and the two definitions contradict. BLOCKING.
partially-acquired turns on an undefined word and contradicts dirty-or-diverged. BLOCKING.
missing-recoverable is unassignable and the blocking-set partition counts it anyway. BLOCKING.
Node absent gives CLEAN and BC-4 has no consumer. BLOCKING.
The marker rule is not applied completely; the falsifier column says where. MAJOR.

BC-8 passes against a hooks directory that does not exist; remedy was assert the directory holds a file. DECLINED by 1.13 section 3.1: a directory holding pre-commit.sh, or pre-commit at mode 100644, satisfies that form and fires nothing. The finding is taken, the remedy is not.
The bootstrap does not detect a fresh clone missing the corpus data files. Add BC-20. MAJOR. Close condition is a date; X2 makes it the Step 1 gate grep.
BC-1's command cannot falsify BC-1's falsifier. MAJOR.
Idempotence is asserted, not assertable, on three counts, one measured. MAJOR.
BC-5 measures the working directory, not the root, and does not enforce its own clause. MINOR.
BC-7's self-deletion clause cannot fire, which makes the clause permanent by accident. MINOR.
BC-14 asserts one of the four markers its own justification names. MINOR.
BC-19 is a fact sitting in a table of assertions; reclassify as fact 3 of the install state record. MINOR.
Section 6's LITERATURE availability is narrower than the answer contract at version 2. MINOR. Depends on AM-66.
The simplicity gate takes the assertion count 19 to 15. The quantity has no block; AM-24 mints it at the value this amendment leaves.
Delete ABORT's second sentence; the outcome line carries ABORT (<phase>, <assertion-id>). 1.5's application of F1.
Define usable: present, and in neither offline nor present-but-wrong. 1.5's application of F2.
Demote missing-recoverable to a Phase 3 transient; it leaves the mode table. 1.5's application of F3.
Q-DEGRADED-MODES 6 to 5, with a superseded entry.
Q-BLOCKING-MODES predicate 3-of-6 to 3-of-5, population 5 rows, with a superseded entry. Its population cell names Q-DEGRADED-MODES, so this lands in the same edit as AM-19.

Assert the hook file exists, is non-empty, begins with #! and carries the marker naming its check register row. OVERRULED at the 1.5/1.13 review X1 in favour of AM-33, which argues explicitly against this form. The marker clause relocates to the check register as CL clause AM-58. This row is the reason the register exists: the ruling was made on 2026-08-27 and had not reached the text.
Measure $ROOT in the shell, not pwd in Node; the long-name clause moves to Phase 1's binding of $ROOT. 1.5's application of F4 and F10.

The reviewer's own list, accepted without restatement and landing in the same edit: BC-4 wired into section 6's origin table; BC-13 merged into BC-12 with two markers; BC-14 asserting all four markers; BC-16 deferred to the sub-step writing the divergence check; BC-3 and BC-15 cut; section 6's LITERATURE and CONTESTED availability conditions split; BC-9's remedy guarded with a --get; the idempotence definition qualified with "and an unchanged upstream"; idempotent replaced by unconditional for Phases 1-6.
Mint Q-BOOTSTRAP-ASSERTIONS, at the value AM-15 leaves. Stated in two files today with no block, so governed by test G1. Deliberately not minted at 1.5 because the value moves in the same week.
Section 1's bare phrase "the four facts" is a second site for Q-STATE-FACTS and comes into <value> [<id>] form under the Tier 2 touch rule.
Replace the five-value verdict table with the two axes of currency policy section 6, with the stated token mapping and three new tokens: withdrawn, behind, diverged.

The direction discriminator is defined only where CURRENCY is upstream-ahead; exit 128 is unknown rather than false. --is-ancestor is reflexive and unguarded accuses the author on every equal session.
git -C <copy> fetch --quiet --prune origin. Without --prune a branch deleted upstream keeps resolving. Measured.
V is the ref of the last row for that copy in oracle/VERIFIED.tsv, which is now append-only.

The idempotence definition's "the timestamp" becomes "written_at and every observed_at" - there are four, and a 6.1 fixture written against the singular reads three violations against a correct implementation.
State idempotence over the right pair of runs: run N+1 is identical to run N in every field but the timestamps, and in every report line, whenever run N wrote no new value to copies. Closes F9b.
Add: never git pull in a working copy. pull is a fetch with a merge attached and the merge is the prohibited half.

Delete BC-8 as written. Replace with: git config core.hooksPath tools/githooks then node tools/checks.js --wiring, running HK-1 and HK-2 of the check register. Every register row naming pre-commit is reported UNWIRED by id on failure. WINS X1 over AM-21.
oracle/VERIFIED.tsv becomes append-only, five columns, # rows=<n>. Seeded content at currency policy section 3.
copies.lsei.head's reader widens to: the next run's Phase 5; the answering loop, as a comparand. The wrongness cell widens and does not weaken.

The consumer count is unchanged at 4. The answering loop already appears; it now reads two fields rather than one. No new consumer, no block correction. Recorded because a reader of the widened section 5 will expect the count to move.
Section 6.1 validates before it branches, so a future record is classified corrupt and overwritten. BLOCKING.
Rule 4 contradicts the write-whole-or-not-at-all rule and the self-check fixture cannot see it. BLOCKING.
Delete pdfs_present: it manufactures the failure it is meant to avoid. Takes Q-STATE-FACTS 4 to 3. MAJOR.
The same edit as AM-39 takes Q-STATE-KEYS 19 to 18.
Section 7's rename guarantee is false under a concurrent reader, and section 7 has no wrongness column. MAJOR.
M1 is not decidable as written: it refuses corpus.digest. MAJOR.
M3 has two readings and the second admits what the first refuses. MAJOR.
written_at's stated reason is false on the file's own text. MINOR.
The keystone holds only on a run that reaches both upstreams, and section 6.2 misreports a deletion. MINOR.
Add CHK-25 (oracle/lib/verify_app_ref.js) and CHK-26 (tools/check_verified_tsv.js), both specified.
CHK-23's asserts and authority cells widen.

Q-CHECK-ROWS 24 to 26 and specified 15 to 17, with a superseded entry. The H row becomes: H 1 <date> 26 7 17 2. COLLIDES with AM-52 and AM-55, which each add a further row after this integer was written as a literal.
CHK-09 asserting HK-1 under CHK-10 dispatch is unbounded recursion. Split CHK-09 into --register and --wiring. BLOCKING.

The consolidation survivor ecr_verify.js could not lift a marked block from a CRLF file, and the silent check produced a wrong verification. The CRLF-tolerant lifter is committed and The Manager verified it at the close. The remaining halves - its absolute require path and the check that cannot fail - are AM-51.
The two remaining halves of R2: ecr_verify.js's absolute require path, and the check that cannot fail.
CL-5(b) is not an expiry; it is a permanent exemption with a name on it. MAJOR.
Four rows carry an invocation in the path cell, and CL-1 fails on quantities.js the day it lands. MAJOR. tools/quantities.js landed at 1.14; see AM-61.
CHK-09 has two invokers wanting two consequences, which its own boundary rule forbids. Lands with AM-49.
CL-6's marker is an English phrase, and CHK-20 is where to set the precedent. MINOR.
CL-6's remedy makes four checks depend on a gitignored working copy, and one of them is on pre-commit. MINOR.
HK-2 asserts the mode bit; nothing asserts the line endings, and the repository commits CR bytes. Commit .gitattributes with tools/githooks/* text eol=lf before installing hooks. MINOR.
Add CL-7(b): an exec-reviewed:<substep> token in authority, so a new row that executes harvested strings and is honestly kinded check has a blocking guard. Uses CL-5's existing device, no new column.
Add CL-8: no row naming pre-commit may contain the literal "git hook run pre-commit". Mechanically checkable. Absorbs the marker clause relocated from AM-21.
Splitting CHK-09 adds one row. Competes with AM-48's literal 26. Named with the real id so AM-1 sees the collision. The Manager rules which successor wins.
tools/quantities.js needs a row, adding one more. Competes with AM-48 and AM-60, all three on Q-CHECK-ROWS.
CONTESTED cannot buy two personas: 10 of 15 lunar axes carry more than two labelled sides. One persona per side, minimum two, no cap.
A one_sided axis cannot produce a CONTESTED verdict. CONTESTED fires on class two_sided or false_pair; one_sided produces LITERATURE or BOTH with a fixed disclosure.
Rule V's CONTESTED row moves findings from Forbidden to permitted-and-never-counted. At least one literature trace per side is unchanged.
The misclassified reason code's condition is container-shaped and is replaced. Owner unchanged and still match_keys.
Contract version 1 becomes 2. The promoted oracle/answer_contract.md line 4 reads "Contract version: 1." today while nine other files read 2. COLLIDES with AM-73.
Every trace line whose origin is app names the lsei ref the value was computed against. Arity unchanged; the ref rides the locator and the origin function strips it.
The ref is read live once per run, git -C lsei rev-parse --short HEAD, never from .oracle-state.json.
The live ref is compared against copies.lsei.head; a mismatch is a report line on the answer.
Every run log row records the app ref, or - where lsei was absent. The row schema is closed, so extending it is a version bump.
An app trace with no ref is a refusal, reason code input-missing, owner the bootstrap. No new reason code.
Section 6's LITERATURE availability condition, narrower than version 2, reconciled from the contract side. Pairs with AM-14.
The run-log schema extension of AM-70 is a third bump, to version 3. COLLIDES with AM-66: two amendments to one integer from two authors, neither aware of the other's arithmetic.

Mint a quantity id for the contract version integer. It is stated in at least eleven files, so it is governed by test G1, and it has no id - which is why AM-1 could not see AM-66 against AM-73 until this register gave them a provisional one by hand.

Q-ROOT-ALLOWANCE names derived-from: Q-PATH-CEILING-259 and no such block exists. M4 reports it as a dangling parent today. Mint the block from the bisection at 1.7 section 8: 259 pass, 260 fail, git 2.55.0.windows.1, core.longpaths unset at all three scopes, OS LongPathsEnabled 0.

Q-ROOT-ALLOWANCE rests on two parents, not one. The second is 108, which is chosen rather than measured (10 + 1 + 32 + 1 + 64) and has no id. Mint it, and add it to derived-from, or the staleness graph cannot see the input most likely to be revisited.

literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv re-admission. The .gitignore half is applied; the NAMING.md half states that the two literals are the corpus's machine-readable files and that a future .tsv is a decision rather than a side effect.
Duplicate id: the block exists in both step1_9 and its addendum. Move, do not copy - COUNTING_RULE.md section 8 permits a block to move between files and does not permit one to exist in two.
Duplicate id, and the two blocks disagree: 58 in step1_9, 59 in the addendum. M3 fails as well as M2.
Duplicate id. Named nowhere before Wave 2.

The worked example cannot be lifted without failing four of its own checks. Add an example namespace: an id beginning Q-EG- is an example, may not be minted as a real block, and is skipped by M2, M3 and M4; and a quantity fence nested inside a four-backtick fence is not a block. HARD.

Section 5 promises a lint that section 7 never mechanizes: a bare governed numeral in a second file. Either specify M13 or delete the row from section 5. tools/quantities.js --lint implements a candidate M13 at 1.14; the contract still has to choose. HARD.

M11 is weaker than the rule it implements and fails on exactly the two blocks that needed it (Q-HOOKSPATH-INERT, Q-REG-TSV-IGNORED). M11 becomes: conditions matches cwd: followed, before the next sentence break, by \d+ characters. Implemented behind --w2-3 at 1.14. HARD.
operation admits three forms and none is arithmetic over other quantities, which derived-from presupposes. Add a fourth form, derived: <expression over ids>, and have M4 evaluate it. HARD.
derived-from's rule becomes: every input to the value, measured or chosen, carries an id. The instance is AM-76. MAJOR.

Section 4's four-part correction has no form for a correction whose sites are in a document another persona has frozen. Add a pending: entry naming the target document and the amendment id in this register. MAJOR. This register is the other half.

Two ids for one quantity and nothing detects it: Q-C4-SOURCE-LEN and Q-C4-SOURCE-LINES are the same 328-line measurement. Delete Q-C4-SOURCE-LEN from 1.12 section 6 and quote Q-C4-SOURCE-LINES. MAJOR.
No form for quoting a range, so M3 cannot read one. 357-686 inclusive [Q-C4-FENCE-SPAN] gives M3 the token "inclusive". MAJOR. 1.14 measures 47 further unreadable-token sites; see the report.

1.6 section 3.5 asked for a clause and it is not in the contract: a file declaring its own size is not a quotation of it. Covers oracle/VERIFIED.tsv's # rows=5, the loose-ends register's 44 rows, the check register's H row, and now MANIFEST.tsv and this file. MAJOR.
The contract states "the nine instances" at five sites and scores itself against nine; step1_author_rulings.md records a tenth three minutes earlier. Run instance 10 against the contract. MINOR.

Two directory-map rows for literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv, added FIRST. Ordering is load-bearing: CHK-12 then fails until the .gitignore re-admission lands, which forces the second half instead of relying on memory.
Re-admit literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv as named literals. Verified at 1.14 by git check-ignore: both tracked; the control probe literature/NAMING.tsv is correctly ignored.

Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum, and the two disagree: 17 against 18. R-6 landed the addendum after the Wave 2 review ran, so this is W2-11's shape repeated in 1.10 and named nowhere. Four siblings follow.
Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.
Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.
Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.
Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.

Two H rows, one file. oracle/register_schema.md section 3.1 says H is one row, the first row, and axis_count is the number of A rows in this file. The lunar and economics halves each carry one H row, naming different basis_root values. Measured at 1.14: the concatenation exits 1 under tools/ecr_verify.js with 143 failure lines. Promoted as two provisional files, oracle/REGISTER.lunar.tsv and oracle/REGISTER.econ.tsv, pending this ruling. NOT The Engineer's to rule.

tools/ecr_verify.js reads the H row as "last H wins" (if(t==='H') H=f) and enforces no cardinality. Against a two-H file it silently validates the second header. The schema says first row and one row; the loader honours neither.

step1_10 and step1_10_addendum carry the SAME marker name, "oracle/REGISTER.tsv (ECR rows)". 1.9's author named the addendum marker distinctly for exactly this reason. A sed naming that marker is ambiguous across files, and the addendum's own section 5 command uses a truncated pattern that matches either. MANIFEST.tsv's MF-3 join is keyed on (source-file, marker) at 1.14 to work around it.

Four deliverables state a lift command with no sed '1d;$d', so the promoted file would begin with its own BEGIN marker, and their post-conditions assert exactly that: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 and 1.13. Three others state the canonical stripping form. 1.14 promoted all eleven with the canonical form the Manager's close section 5.4 quotes. The four post-conditions are now false against the promoted files and need amending or the ruling needs reversing.

The declared file set is amended to exclude cr_scratch blocks whose target has been promoted, or the promotion's own first defect is a duplicate-id failure. MEASURED at 1.14: promotion took hard failures from 23 to 33; the eight new ones are exactly the eight blocks predicted (Q-BOOTSTRAP-PHASES, Q-DEGRADED-MODES, Q-BLOCKING-MODES, Q-STATE-FACTS, Q-STATE-ABNORMAL-READS, Q-STATE-CONSUMERS, Q-STATE-KEYS, Q-PAIR-IDENTICAL). tools/quantities.js --exclude-superseded implements the amendment and returns the count to 24.

tools/quantities.js exists as of 1.14, so CL-2 requires all four of its rows to move from specified to live. Measured: CL-2 reports four failures on those rows today, plus CHK-23 whose path oracle/bootstrap_contract.md is now promoted.

Add CHK-27 (tools/check_registers.js --manifest, MF-1 to MF-3) and CHK-28 (--amendments, AM-1 to AM-4). CL-1 fails today: tools/check_registers.js is under the tools/** scan root with no row. Ids 27 and 28 are chosen to leave 25 and 26 to AM-46.

R4 confirmed by strict measurement: a CL-1 join on literal paths fails on tools/quantities.js because its four rows carry invocations (tools/quantities.js --check) in the path cell rather than a path. Two files fail strict CL-1 today; only one of them is genuinely unregistered.
Adding CHK-27 and CHK-28 is a fourth competing successor to Q-CHECK-ROWS. Recorded so AM-1 shows all four rather than three.
